title: Human rights & the UDHR
examples: What does 'universal' mean when we talk about human rights?
Can you give an example of a right that everyone should have?
Who made the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?

explain.say: Today we learn about human rights for everyone.

items: They are important for a good life.
They are shared by all people.

explain.say: Universal rights mean rights for every single person.
The UDHR lists many basic rights for all humans.
These rights protect us from unfair treatment by others.
A right to education means you should learn at school.
In daily life, your right to speak your mind matters.

faq.a: They are called universal because they belong to every single person, no matter where they live. You might also hear this called 'for all people' or 'human rights for everyone.'
asks: Do all people have the same rights?

faq.q: What does it mean to have a right to education?
faq.a: It means that every person has the right to learn and go to school. This helps people build knowledge and a better future. You could also ask about 'the right to learn' or 'schooling rights.'
asks: Does everyone get to go to school?

faq.a: They are protected by laws and international agreements, like the UDHR. These rules stop people from being treated unfairly. You might ask about 'rights protection' or 'keeping rights safe.'
asks: What stops people from breaking rights?

faq.q: Are human rights different for different groups of people?
faq.a: No, human rights are the same for everyone. They do not depend on your nationality, gender, or background. This is the core idea of universality. You could ask if rights are 'equal for all' or 'the same everywhere.'
asks: Do only some people have rights?
Are rights only for certain groups?

faq.a: The UDHR stands for the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. It is a very important document listing basic rights. You could also ask about 'the declaration of rights' or 'what is the UDHR?'
asks: What is the big book of rights?
Where did the UDHR come from?

facts: Human rights are inherent; they belong to you just because you are human.
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was a major global agreement.
These rights protect fundamental aspects of human dignity.
Rights like freedom of speech are crucial for a functioning society.

quiz.say: If a country stops teaching its citizens, which right is being violated?

options.show: The right to education is a universal right.
options.say: The right to education is a universal right.

quiz.why: The right to education is a fundamental right that every person should have access to learning.

wrong.0: Travel rights relate to movement, not the ability to learn.
wrong.2: Voting is important, but the right to education is about learning itself.
wrong.3: Property rights are different from the right to access knowledge.

quiz.say: Which word best describes rights that belong to every single person?
quiz.why: Universal means something applies everywhere and to everyone, which is the definition of human rights.

wrong.0: Temporary means it only lasts for a short time.
wrong.2: Local means only in one small area, not everywhere.
wrong.3: Optional means you can choose if you want it, but rights are not choices.

quiz.say: If a government treats one group of people unfairly, which concept is being ignored?
quiz.why: Universal rights stress that these rights apply equally to all people without exception.

wrong.0: National rights suggest rights only come from a specific country.
wrong.1: Group rights suggest some people have rights that others do not.
wrong.2: Conditional rights suggest rights can be taken away if you do something wrong.
